subsystems.name: Alloy chemistry
subsystems.role: sets the transformation temperature and the amount of force the alloy can generate.
parts: near-equiatomic nickel and titanium (roughly 50–51 atomic % nickel)
ternary additions such as copper, iron, niobium or hafnium to tune the transition

subsystems.name: Phase microstructure
subsystems.role: the two crystal structures whose switch is the whole mechanism — a stiff austenite and a soft, easily deformed martensite.
parts: precipitates used to strengthen the alloy

subsystems.name: Forming and drawing
subsystems.role: turns an ingot into the wire, tube, sheet or bar a device needs.

subsystems.name: Shape-setting heat treatment
subsystems.role: fixes the shape the alloy will remember.
parts: fixture that holds the part in its target form

subsystems.name: Actuation and control
subsystems.role: delivers the heat or stress that triggers the change.
parts: Joule heating from an electric current
bias spring or superelastic element for a return stroke

buildSteps.title: Melt the alloy
buildSteps.detail: Nickel and titanium are melted together under vacuum, then re-melted by arc to drive out impurities such as oxygen and carbon that would embrittle the metal.

buildSteps.title: Cast an ingot
buildSteps.detail: The melt is poured into a mould and cooled; the resulting ingot is checked for composition and homogeneity.

buildSteps.title: Hot work the ingot
buildSteps.detail: At roughly 800–900 °C the ingot is forged, rolled or extruded into bar, sheet or tube stock.

buildSteps.title: Cold draw to final size
buildSteps.detail: Wire is pulled through successively smaller dies, with anneals in between, down to the tenths of a millimetre used in guidewires and stents.

buildSteps.title: Form the component
buildSteps.detail: The stock is wound into coils, laser-cut into stent lattices, or machined — difficult work, because the alloy work-hardens rapidly.

buildSteps.title: Set the remembered shape
buildSteps.detail: The part is clamped in a fixture, held at several hundred degrees, then cooled, leaving it with a memory of that geometry.

buildSteps.title: Train the behaviour
buildSteps.detail: Repeated heating and loading cycles stabilise the transformation temperatures and the fatigue life.

buildSteps.title: Finish and verify
buildSteps.detail: Electropolishing smooths the surface, and calorimetry confirms the transformation temperatures are where the design needs them.

prerequisites.why: titanium is reactive and tiny oxygen or carbon levels ruin the transformation.

prerequisites.tech: Control of the nickel–titanium phase diagram
prerequisites.why: a change of one atomic percent of nickel shifts the transformation temperature by many degrees.
the remembered shape and the working temperature are both set by the anneal.

prerequisites.tech: Fine wire drawing and laser micromachining
prerequisites.why: stents and guidewires are made at sub-millimetre scale.
an implant must survive millions of cycles inside the body without releasing nickel.

pathway.milestone: nickel–titanium (Nitinol) stents, guidewires, orthodontic archwires and aerospace couplings
pathway.unlocks: devices that deploy themselves inside the body or seal a joint without a motor.

pathway.milestone: solid-state elastocaloric cooling, where cycling the alloy under stress pumps heat
high-temperature alloys such as nickel–titanium–hafnium, working above 100 °C
pathway.unlocks: actuators in engines and industrial machinery that replace motors and hydraulics.

pathway.milestone: cheap iron-based alloys and magnetic shape memory materials at scale
pathway.unlocks: damping and prestressing in civil structures, and fast, silent magnetic actuators.
